claims.text: The initial PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a nanoscale solid solution with a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Ethanol oxidation for this catalyst is typically conducted within 0.2–0.8 V vs. RHE at ambient temperature in aqueous ethanol.
The controlled intervention is a slight increase in applied potential using potential pulses relative to an unmodulated lower-potential baseline.
A slight increase in applied potential induces dynamic surface segregation in the PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst.
The potential-induced segregation specifically enriches Ru at the catalyst surface.
The potential-induced segregation specifically enriches Rh at the catalyst surface.
Changes in surface composition alter the local electronic structure of a multielement alloy catalyst.
Ru/Rh surface enrichment changes the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The modified intermediate binding energies favor partial ethanol oxidation over complete oxidation.
The potential increase shifts product selectivity toward acetic acid rather than CO2.
The potential-induced surface state facilitates formation of a self-limiting oxide/hydroxide layer.
The oxide/hydroxide layer protects the catalyst and improves durability.
Relative to the baseline, potential pulsing will produce measurably greater Ru/Rh surface enrichment.
Relative to the baseline, potential pulsing will increase catalyst activity retention over time.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold only under ambient aqueous ethanol-oxidation conditions within 0.2–0.8 V vs. RHE.
Very high potentials may cause excessive oxidation and therefore depart from the predicted trend.
Very low potentials may fail to induce Ru/Rh segregation.
Absence of statistically significant Ru/Rh enrichment together with no product shift and no durability improvement relative to baseline would falsify the proposed mechanism.
